## R primer {#r-primer}

A mandatory R primer precedes the course and sets a common baseline. Please work through it before the first session.

- R and RStudio: installation, projects, scripts
- Data import and data frames
- Data wrangling with `dplyr` and `tidyr`
- Plotting with `ggplot2`
- Reproducible reports with Quarto

Recommended free material: Wickham, H., Çetinkaya-Rundel, M., & Grolemund, G. (2023). *R for data science* (2nd ed.). <https://r4ds.hadley.nz/>

## Books

- Gelman, A., Hill, J., & Vehtari, A. (2020). *Regression and other stories.* Cambridge University Press. Free PDF: <https://avehtari.github.io/ROS-Examples/>
- Fox, J. (2016). *Applied regression analysis and generalized linear models* (3rd ed.). Sage.
- Fox, G. A., Negrete-Yankelevich, S., & Sosa, V. J. (Eds.). (2015). *Ecological statistics: Contemporary theory and application.* Oxford University Press.
- McElreath, R. (2020). *Statistical rethinking* (2nd ed.). CRC Press.
- Lakens, D. *Improving your statistical inferences.* <https://lakens.github.io/statistical_inferences/>

## R packages used in the course

| Package | Used for |
|---|---|
| `tidyverse` | data handling and plotting |
| `emmeans` | estimated marginal means and contrasts |
| `car` | ANOVA tables, variance inflation factors |
| `performance`, `DHARMa` | model diagnostics |
| `lme4`, `glmmTMB` | mixed models |
| `rpact` | sequential designs (course *Open, Replicable, and Ethical Science*) |
| `TOSTER`, `BayesFactor`, `brms`, `bayestestR` | equivalence tests and Bayesian alternatives (course *Testing for Absence and Equivalence*) |

## Data

All datasets used on this site are in the [`data/`](https://github.com/SimonStephan31/cbbstats/tree/main/data) folder of the repository, each with a short description.
